cards.title: Introduction to Caching
cards.content:
Caching is a technique of storing frequently accessed data in a temporary storage location (cache) to reduce the latency and load on the database or external services.

In ASP.NET Core, caching improves application performance and scalability significantly.

cards.title: In-Memory Caching
cards.content:
In-Memory caching stores data in the memory of the web server hosting the ASP.NET Core application.

It is best suited for single-server environments and uses the built-in IMemoryCache interface.

public class MyService {
    private readonly IMemoryCache _cache;
    public MyService(IMemoryCache cache) => _cache = cache;
}

cards.title: Distributed Caching
cards.content:
In web farms or cloud environments with multiple server instances, in-memory caches are not shared. Distributed caching solves this by maintaining a cache external to the app servers (e.g., Redis or SQL Server).

It uses the IDistributedCache interface.

cards.title: Response Caching Middleware
cards.content:
Response caching adds headers like Cache-Control to HTTP responses, instructing clients, proxies, or servers on how to cache responses.

Register it in Program.cs using app.UseResponseCaching();.

cards.title: Cache Expiration Strategies
cards.content:
To prevent stale data, ASP.NET Core supports two main types of expiration:

  • Absolute Expiration: Removes the item after a fixed time period.
  • Sliding Expiration: Extends the expiration timer each time the item is accessed.

cards.title: Conclusion and Best Practices
cards.content:
Always consider your deployment environment (single server vs. web farm) when choosing between IMemoryCache and IDistributedCache.

Use appropriate expiration policies to prevent memory leaks and ensure data freshness.
